newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia launches U.S. communication satellite.
newsitem.headline: Russia launches U.S. communication satellite.

text.p: Russia's Proton-K heavy booster on Saturday successfully sent into orbit a U.S. Telstar-5 telecommunication satellite, a mission control official said.
"The Proton-K rocket blasted off at 9 p.m. Moscow time (1700 GMT) from the Baikonur cosmodrome in Kazakhstan," the official told Reuters.
The 3,650 kg Telstar-5 probe was produced by U.S. Space System Loral Inc to provide television coverage to Alaska, Hawaii and Puerto Rico as well as to Canada and Mexico.
The probe will move round the Earth at an altitude of 36,000 km (22,500 miles), the official said. He did not say how much money the launch had cost.
"It was the first Proton booster launch since a similar rocket crashed in November of last year when it tried to send a Russian probe to Mars," a spokesman for the military space forces said.

An official at the Russian rocket maker Khrunichev Space Centre, which produces Proton rockets, said Russian insurance company Ingosstrakh had provided $500 million in liability coverage for the centre and its partners to launch the satellite.
Khrunichev's spokesman recently said that Proton rockets would lift into orbit a total of eight Western-made satellites by the end of this year, up from two probes in 1996.

The centre has signed a total of 20 contracts worth $1.5 billion, including for the planned piece-by-piece construction of the international orbiting station Alpha, which will replace Russia's ageing Mir station.
